To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

alloxan, when administered to the 3v of rats, impairs counterregulatory responses to both systemic (2DG) and hindbrain glucopenia (5-thio-gluc) and that this impairment is associated with destruction of tanycytes and reduced expression of NPY and POMC in the ARC.
3v alloxan reverses glucoprivic responses, and that this is associated with the destruction and subsequent recovery of 3v neurons and tanycytes.

alloxan, an inhibitor and toxin of GK, injected into the third ventricular (3v) of rats reversibly impairs counterregulatory responses to systemic and hindbrain (arcuate nucleus) glucoprivation, which is associated with 3v tanicyte destruction and decreased NPY mRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the hypothalamus in the control of food intake and glucose metabolism.
the role of the third ventrile in the regulation of feeding behavior.
the role of the third ventricular tanycyte in the control of feeding and counterregulatory responses to glucoprivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3v tanocytes and the surrounding neurons play a critical role in the glucoprivic counter-regulatory response.
3v tanocytes, but not hypothalamic neurons, are the primary targets of 3v alloxan and the primary mediators of these glucoprivational responses.
3v tanocytes and/or other neurons are involved in the expression and/or maintenance of the glucoprivic feeding, hyperglycemia, and hyperinsulinemia responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3v is a critical brain region for the expression of glucoprivic counter-regulatory responses.
alloxan reverses glucosensing in the third ventrile and impairs glucoprivic counter-regulatory responses.
the 3v tanocytes and the neurons around the 3V are critically involved in the glucoprivic counter-regulatory responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GK may be a critical component of the glucosensing system in the hypothalamus, but the role of GK may be more complex than originally hypothesized.
the third ventricular region is critical for the expression of glucoprivic counter-regulatory responses.
glucokinase in the brain is important for the expression of glucoprivic counter-regulatory responses.
